title: We Are South Maui: Community Plan Advisory Committee Meeting of April 12, 2023

recap.headline: South Maui plan committee finishes policy review and ranks every plan action
recap.in_60_seconds: The South Maui Community Plan Advisory Committee met to finish reviewing draft policies and actions and to set priorities for each action. There was no public testimony because the meeting resumed after a recess; about 11 committee members and 2 planning staff spoke. Members adopted wording changes on shoreline restrooms, sewer extension in Mākena, dune management staffing, water quality monitoring, cesspool conversion dates and the County wetlands mapping study. They added new actions to fund a study on restoring Puʻu Hale, to find land for cultural centers and museums in Kula Kai and Honuaʻula Kai, and to create a green waste and compost program. They then rated every action high, medium or low, with most rated high or medium. Proposals on shipping recyclables off island and cutting single-use plastics were deferred, and land use work starts next week.

parts.title: Roll call, announcements and schedule
presented: Quorum confirmed; two members excused.
A member disclosed that at least three members attended the County Council budget hearing in Kīhei as individuals, not as committee business.
Members agreed with no objection to invite the mayor and cabinet members, including the housing director, to a future meeting.
The committee is one week behind its adopted schedule; the Council approved an extension of up to a year.

next.what: Invite the mayor and housing director to speak

parts.title: Reading of the South Maui vision statement
presented: Vision read from page 9 of the draft plan: restored beaches and wetlands, affordable housing near jobs, safe walking and biking paths, protected cultural resources.

parts.title: Shoreline restrooms and Mākena sewer extension
presented: Added the word gulches to two watershed actions under 2.4.5.
Reworded the shoreline restroom policy so it does not encourage new shoreline development; it is about keeping waste out of the ocean.
Several members said Mākena State Park is dangerous and should stay a wilderness park; one member called for a true carrying capacity study.
Adopted an action to fund extending the Mākena wastewater system and connect properties on on-site waste disposal systems as far as feasible, with the state park reference removed.

answered.said: The official term is on-site waste disposal systems, which covers both cesspools and septic systems.
Shoreline policy language can only encourage, not require, because the plan cannot mandate it.

parts.title: Watershed, dunes, water quality and cesspool actions
presented: Action 4.02 now says the plan is updated in consultation with Native Hawaiian organizations; 'where feasible' removed.
A regional stormwater park was placed mauka of Pi’ilani Highway to address North Kīhei flooding.
Funding expanded for additional dune management coordinator positions and sand dune protection; water quality monitoring to follow a Department of Health quality assurance plan.

Cesspool language corrected: the state working group urges Maui Meadows conversion by 2035, but the committee still asks for 2030; one member recused. 'Such as' removed from the list of land parcels to acquire.

parts.title: Wetlands study, Puʻu Hale and cultural centers
presented: Removed 'or other similar studies' so the plan relies on the County wetlands mapping study.
New action to fund a study for restoring Puʻu Hale, with Native Hawaiian organizations consulted.
New action to find locations and funding and build cultural centers and museums in Kula Kai and Honuaʻula Kai; members noted South Maui has none.
One member spoke about the cost of living and respect for the host culture while supporting the motion.

answered.said: The wetlands ordinance calls for the study to be updated about every five years.
Proposed language to fund a restoration study for Puʻu Hale.

parts.title: Green waste, recycling and plastics proposals
presented: Adopted a new action to develop a green waste collection and compost utilization program in section 2.2.
A member said Kīhei Compost may close this year and $250,000 was requested at the budget hearing to keep it open.
A proposal for a partnership to ship recyclables off island drew debate about reducing waste first and was deferred.
A third idea, a partnership with airlines and hotels to cut single-use plastic, was put forward for later.

next.what: Revised recycling and single-use plastic action language brought back
Further review of policies and actions, including submitted testimony

parts.title: Prioritizing actions in sections 1 and 2
presented: Members started from the pre-meeting poll result for each action, then moved and voted.
Pedestrian safety, affordable housing infrastructure, shoreline access and park actions mostly rated high.
Members debated whether too many actions are high; a few, including 1.14, 1.17a and 2.01, were rated low.
Campsites rated medium because they have been in the 1998 plan for 25 years without action.

parts.title: Prioritizing actions in sections 3, 4 and 5
presented: Most hazard, watershed and cultural actions rated high; wildfire data action rated medium because the current fire chief does not see it as a priority.
A member asked staff to show which County departments are assigned to each action so priorities can be balanced at the next review.
The archaeological inventory was rated high; a member said the last one was in 1974.
One member recused on Maui Meadows items.

next.what: Staff to show department assignments for each action

parts.title: Closing
presented: All flagged policies and actions were reviewed and all actions prioritized; meeting closed at 8:55 p.m.

open_questions.question: Is the Mākena wastewater treatment plant still privately owned?
Will County funding keep Kīhei Compost open, and where would South Maui green waste go if it closes?
Which County departments are responsible for each high-priority action?
Will the state fund a carrying capacity study for Mākena State Park?

not_on_tracker.topic: Mākena State Park safety and visitor capacity
not_on_tracker.why: Members said the beach causes serious spinal injuries and more amenities could draw more visitors.
Losing it would leave South Maui landscapers and farmers without green waste composting.

not_on_tracker.topic: Cesspool conversion in Maui Meadows and Māʻalaea
not_on_tracker.why: Members said cesspools add nutrients to coastal waters and want conversion by 2030.
The puʻu is culturally significant to South Maui, Māʻalaea and Waikapū.

not_on_tracker.topic: Cultural center and museum for South Maui
not_on_tracker.why: South Maui has no place to display artifacts or practice and share Hawaiian culture.

not_on_tracker.topic: Island waste, recycling and single-use plastics
not_on_tracker.why: Members are concerned about the landfill filling up and waste brought in by visitors.

moments.who: South Maui Community Plan Advisory Committee chair
moments.quote: So we're going to need to speed up a little bit here if we're going to finish by the end of June.
moments.about: The chair said the advisory committee was a week behind its adopted schedule for drafting the South Maui Community Plan, and it aimed to finish by the end of June.

moments.who: South Maui Community Plan Advisory Committee member
moments.quote: Bathroom at McKenna State Park, it's going to invite a lot more people to come over there. And my biggest thing over there is safety. And that beach has caused, I think, the most spinal injuries in all of Hawaiʻi.
moments.about: A committee member warned that restrooms at Mākena State Park would draw more visitors to a beach known for serious shorebreak injuries.

moments.who: South Maui Community Plan Advisory Committee member
moments.quote: People don't think of Makena as having wetlands, but they do. There's one by ʻOneuli, Black Sand, and two behind ʻOneloa.
moments.about: A committee member raised environmental risks to three wetlands inside Mākena State Park from new wastewater infrastructure.

moments.who: South Maui Community Plan Advisory Committee member and former Oneloa Coalition participant
moments.quote: We need to do a capacity study, which we have been encouraging for years, and not how many parking stalls can we put in as a capacity, but a true capacity study. What can this park sustain?
moments.about: A committee member urged a true carrying-capacity study for Mākena State Park rather than planning around the number of parking stalls.

moments.who: South Maui Community Plan Advisory Committee vice chair
moments.quote: And there was a real debate about putting in permanent bathrooms and showers there. And that's been debated for years. The park was originally meant to be a wilderness park.
moments.about: The vice chair recalled years of debate over permanent restrooms and showers at Mākena and said the park was meant to stay a wilderness park.

moments.who: County Planning staff reading adopted language
moments.quote: Fund the extension of the McKenna wastewater infrastructure and connect all properties as far as feasible that are currently on-site waste disposal systems to the extended sewer line.
moments.about: This is the final wording the committee adopted for a plan action to extend Mākena sewer service to homes now on cesspools or septic systems.

moments.who: South Maui Community Plan Advisory Committee chair
moments.quote: It urges them by 2035. So we're just acknowledging that. We're still keeping what we want, which is we want to convert them all by 2030.
moments.about: The draft plan was corrected to cite the state's 2035 cesspool deadline while still calling for Maui Meadows cesspools to be converted by 2030.

moments.who: South Maui Community Plan Advisory Committee member
moments.quote: But we don't have a cultural center or a museum Anywhere in South Maui.
moments.about: A committee member made the case for a new plan action to fund cultural centers and museums in Kūlanihākoʻi and Honuaʻula.
